proposal.summary: Multiple Draytek products use hardcoded encryption keys that allow attackers to bind affected devices to attacker-controlled accounts, then create and synchronize WCF and DrayDDNS licenses from the website.
proposal.affected_product: Draytek Vigor Routers < 3.9.6 / 4.2.4; Access Points < v1.4.0; Switches < 2.6.7; Myvigor < 2.3.2
proposal.cwe_quote: were discovered to use hardcoded encryption keys

AV.quote: were discovered to use hardcoded encryption keys which allows attackers to bind any affected device to their own account.

PR.quote: allows attackers to bind any affected device to their own account.

C.quote: Attackers are then able to create WCF and DrayDDNS licenses and synchronize them from the website.

I.quote: Attackers are then able to create WCF and DrayDDNS licenses and synchronize them from the website.

A.quote: Attackers are then able to create WCF and DrayDDNS licenses and synchronize them from the website.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Verify affected firmware versions and reproduce binding using the reported hardcoded keys; obtain exact proof text or sample request showing binding and license synchronization to assess full impact and prepare patch/mitigation.
